items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Public method names are clear, but the internal types (durabilityManager, jobDurabilityState, durabilitySub) have no comments. The long `d.durability.mu.` chains and the unexplained `if syncDur <= 0 { syncDur = time.Nanosecond }` clamp, repeated many times in commit.go, make the code harder to follow.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The 1ns clamp block is copy-pasted 5 times in Commit. WaitForDurabilityContext repeats its done/err/closed checks in the ctx.Done branch, and the job wait duplicates them again. Durability logic is spread across batch.go (signalDurable), db.go and durability.go instead of living in one tracker type.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: batchInternal.durableOnce (a sync.Once) is apparently never reset (no reset change shown), so a reused batch would never fire again. SyncDuration is timed from before prepare and clamped to a fake 1ns. Once the job window is full, registerPendingJob scans the whole map on every commit. Errors are not swallowed.

items.name: Commit path and public types remain backward compatible
items.name_zh: 提交路径与公共类型保持向后兼容
items.evidence: The new APIs are additive. However, every NoSyncWait commit now spawns a goroutine (`go func(...){ b.fsyncWait.Wait() ...}`). Every sync commit takes a mutex and allocates a notifyCh even when BatchDurable is unset. applyInternal now sets `batch.db = d`, and the error-path `b.db = nil` handling moved.
